## Description

The ship is equipped with a full-scale TL4 fabrication plant programmed to support its needs. The ship can stock raw materials and parts at 5000 credits per ton; these parts can then be used to "pay" ship repair or maintenance costs when conventional shipyards are unavailable. The factory can also create repair vehicles, TL4 equipment, space habs, and planetary structures with these parts at a rate of 10000 credits worth of construction a day. If a [[Mobile extractor|mobile extractor]] is available, the raw materials processed by the latter unit can be used to feed the factory. Operating a mobile factory requires at least 100 well-trained personnel. Each 10 fewer doubles repair or maintenance times.

name: Observation Suite

| Property | Value |

All drones are wired for basic camera and sound, but this suite contains a full-spectrum UV/IR visual package, remote sound sensors, and radiation/chemical detectors. The drone can focus on conversations or facial expressions from up to 2 kilometers away and can operate even in the complete absence of visible light.

name: Precognitive nav chamber
body:
| Property | Value |

## Description

An extremely rare example of psitech dating from before the Scream, a precognitive nav chamber allows a character with at least [[Precognition|Precognition]]-2 psionic skill to assist in interstellar drills, sensing impending shear alterations before they happen. The navigator automatically succeeds on any spike drill check of difficulty 9 or less. On a failed check, add 2 to the Spike Drive Mishap roll, limiting the potential damage. On drilling in to the destination system, the psychic has expended all Effort in the process.

name: Psionic anchorpoint
body:
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Cost** | Free |
| **Power** | 3 |
| **Mass** | 0 |
| **Min Class** | Frigate |
| **TL** | 4 |
| **Effect** | Focal point for allied psychics' [[Powers\|powers]] |

## Description

This pretech relic is unavailable on the open market in most sectors. Once installed in a ship, it can be "imprinted" by up to a dozen psychics. These psychics can sense and affect any object or location within ten meters of the relic after one minute of concentration, provided they are within the same solar system. Thus, teleporters can always teleport next to the anchorpoint, telepaths can always contact anyone within the affected zone, telekinetics can manipulate objects near the relic, and so forth. The relic can be re-coded to eliminate existing imprints, but any psychic wo gets access to the relic for ten minutes of meditation and focus can imprint on it afterwards. There is no obvious way to tell how many psychics have imprinted to the anchorpoint.

The ship can disguise its long-range sensor readings, spoofing scans with the ID tags and apparent hull type of any other ship of its choice. To penetrate this masquerade, the scanning entity must beat a Wis/Program skill check against difficulty 10 plus the Program skill of the masking ship's comms officer. Once the ship is close enough to visually identify, the masking is useless.

The drone is sheathed in anti-radar composites. Ordinary sensors will not detect it at observation range, and high-end military sensors can spot it only on an Int/Program check at difficulty 9.

name: Ship bay (fighter)
body:

| **Min Class** | Cruiser |
| **TL** | 4 |

## Description

These sophisticated docking bays provide all the necessary tools and support for launching a starship from the mother craft. They are rarely seen outside of dedicated capital-class carriers, but some cruisers make room to mount a fighter-class attack shuttle. Each bay allows room for one ship of the appropriate hull class. While the carried ship can support its own crew if necessary, most carriers fold their space wing into the mothership's crew roster. This fitting can be taken multiple times.

## Description

These sophisticated docking bays provide all the necessary tools and support for launching a starship from the mother craft. They are rarely seen outside of dedicated capital-class carriers, but some cruisers make room to mount a fighter-class attack shuttle. Each bay allows room for one ship of the appropriate hull class. While the carried ship can support its own crew if necessary, most carriers fold their space wing into the mothership's crew roster. This fitting can be taken multiple times.

name: Ship's locker
body:
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Cost** | 2,000 credits |
| **Power** | 0 |
| **Mass** | 0 |
| **Min Class** | Frigate |
| **TL** | 4 |
| **Effect** | General equipment for the crew |

## Description

Much like an [[Armory|armory]], this option allows a captain to lay in a general supply of equipment likely to be useful to explorers and spacemen. Any TL4 equipment on the gear list can be found in the ship's locker in amounts commensurate with the ship's size. A few guns and some basic [[Armor|armor]] might be included as well, but for serious armament an [[Armory|armory]] is required. There is enough gear available to outfit the entire crew for normal use, but giving it away or losing it in use may deplete the locker until it is restocked.

name: Shiptender mount
body:
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Cost** | 25,000 credits |
| **Power** | 1 |
| **Mass** | 1 |
| **Min Class** | Frigate |
| **TL** | 4 |
| **Effect** | Allow another ship to hitch on a spike drive |

## Description

The ship is designed with symbiosis mounts that allow other ships to "hitch" on the crat's spike drills. Each shiptender mount allows one craft of a hull size smaller than the tender to link up for intersystem drills. Mounts cannot be used for in-system travel. If the linking ship has been designed to be carried by a tender then establishing this link takes one hour. If not, it takes a full day to fit the ship into the mount. Ships can dismount from the tender with an hour's disentanglement. In an emergency, the carried ship can dismount instnatly, but the mountings are considered disable then until repairs are made. Carried ships cannot fight.

name: Smuggler's hold
body:
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Cost** | 2,500 credits |
| **Power** | 0 |
| **Mass** | 1 |
| **Min Class** | Fighter |
| **TL** | 4 |
| **Effect** | Small amount of well-hidden [[Cargo space\|cargo space]] |

## Description

Carefully-designed storage space intended to conceal illicit cargo from customs inspection. Each installation of this fitting adds 200 kilograms of [[Cargo space|cargo space]] in a fighter, 2 tons in a frigate, 20 tons in a cruiser, or 200 tons in a capital ship. Cargo in smuggler's hold will never be found by a standard customs inspection. Careful investigation by a suspicious official can find it on a difficulty 10 check using their Wis/[[Notice|Notice]] skill, and a week-long search one step short of disassembly will find it on a difficulty 7 check.

name: Stationkeeping
body:
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Cost** | 1,000 credits |
| **Power** | 0 |
| **Mass** | 1 |
| **Min Class** | Fighter |
| **TL** | 4 |

## Description

The drone does not need to be constantly controlled; when the operator does not spend a Main Action to pilot it, it simply remains stationary. If equipped with an [[Observation Suite|Observation Suite]], it can ping the operator if any anomalous reading is obtained.

name: Suicide Charge
body:
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Cost** | 250 credits |
| **Power** | 0 |
| **Mass** | 1 |
| **Min Class** | Fighter |
| **TL** | 3 |

## Description

The drone is loaded with a [[Demo Charge|demo charge]] as per page 69. The operator can trigger it as an attack, but unless they can move the drone in by surprise, the approach will always give onlookers a chance to spot it before it gets within range.

name: Survey sensor array
body:
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Cost** | 5,000 credits |
| **Power** | 2 |
| **Mass** | 1 |
| **Min Class** | Frigate |
| **TL** | 4 |
| **Effect** | Improved planetary sensory array |

## Description

Most ships require only basic analysis of a star system, sufficient to identify population centers, do rough scanning of an object's composition, and char major navigational hazards. Survey sensor arrays greatly enhance the ship's sensor abilities, allowing for finely-detailed mapping of objects and planets, along with broad spectrum [[Communications|communications]] analysis. They also improve attempts to detect other craft when scanning a region for stealthy vessels. Any rolls with survey sensor arrays add +2 to skill checks.

name: System Drive
body:
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Cost** | Free |
| **Power** | 0 |
| **Mass** | 0 |
| **Min Class** | Fighter |
| **TL** | 4 |
| **Effect** | Replace spike drive with small system drive |

## Description

The ship’s standard drive-1 spike drive is removed and replaced with a different propulsion system. The ship is still treated as having a drive-1 for maneuvering and system transit purposes, but it cannot make interstellar drills. This modification  lowers the cost of the basic hull by 10% and adds extra power and space based on the size of the hull: 1 power for fighters, 2 for frigates, 3 for cruisers, and 4 for capital ship hulls. Twice this amount of free mass is gained by the process.

name: Teleportation pads
body:
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Cost** | 200,000 credits |
| **Power** | 1 |
| **Mass** | 1 |
| **Min Class** | Frigate |
| **TL** | 4 |
| **Effect** | Pretech [[Teleportation\|teleportation]] to and from ship |

## Description

This TL5 tech is completely unavailable in most sectors and was uncommon even on Mandate-era ships. The pads allow up to a dozen people or 1200 kilograms of matter to be teleported to and from the surface of a planet or the interior of another ship, provided it is no more than a few tens of thousands of kilometers distant. Ship-to-ship [[Teleportation|teleportation]] is possible only when the receiving ship is cooperating by transmitting accurate coordinate details; otherwise, a friendly unjammed signal from inside is necessary to lock onto the target point. Planetary teleportations are possible only in the absence of physical barriers between the ship and the target point below. The teleporters may be used once every five minutes. In those rare sectors where this tech is widely available, it costs 200k.

name: Tractor beams
body:
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Cost** | 10,000 credits |
| **Power** | 2 |
| **Mass** | 1 |
| **Min Class** | Frigate |
| **TL** | 4 |
| **Effect** | Manipulate objects in space at a distance |

## Description

Gravitic projectors allow the ship to manipulate objects within its immediate area, pushing, pulling, and sliding objects no larger than a ship of one hull class smaller. Targets with ship-scale propulsion can resist the beams, but [[Lifeboats|lifeboats]], individual suit jets, or other smaller propulsors are inadequate. The beam can focus only on one Object at a time but can move it into the ship's cargo bays or hurl it out of the ship's immediate vicinity within three rounds. The beams can only effectively manipulate objects in very low gravity, and not those on the surface of planets or other objects with significant natural gravity.

name: Vehicle transport fittings
body:
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Cost** | 2,500 credits |
| **Power** | 0 |
| **Mass** | 1 |
| **Min Class** | Frigate |
| **TL** | 4 |
| **Effect** | Halve tonnage space of carried vehicles |

## Description

The ship has been fitted with specialized mounts, bunking, cargo bays, and other facilities to expedite the transport of often unwieldy vehicles, including including mechs and other military craft. Any vehicles carried count as only half their usual cargo tonnage. Assuming trained operators, up to four vehicles can be offloaded or ramped onto the ship per round in cases where speed is critical.

name: Weapon Fitting

| Property | Value |

| **TL** | 3 |

The drone can be mounted with 1 encumbrance worth of [[Ranged|ranged]] weaponry, which must be purchased separately. This fitting may be taken more than once to mount more weapons or heavier weapons. The weapon requires one or more ammo units to feed it.

name: Workshop
body:
| Property | Value |

| **Power** | 1 |
| **Mass** | 1 |

## Description

Built off the biggest hull class that TL4 polities can create, only the richest modern worlds can afford to fabricate these massive engines of war. Even those worlds with adequate resources to do so often balk at expending such a tremendous amount of money on a single ship. Those that do build battleships do so for a reason. The tremendous weight of fire these ships put out can pop a cruiser in a single firing pass, and its reinforced hull plating shrugs off all but the heaviest [[Armor|armor]]-piercing blows. Where cruisers often require hunter-killer frigates to take them out, battleships commonly require hunter-killer cruisers to disable them.  The main weakness of a battleship is the fact that it is only a single ship… a single, extremely expensive ship. It can only attack or defend a single location at a time, and an enemy that has the time and resources to build specialized anti-capital ships with AP weaponry and expendable crews can bring the battleship down for far less money than it cost to build it.

## Defenses

### [[Hardened Polyceramic Overlay|Hardened Polyceramic Overlay]]

A complex glazing process can harden the surface of a ship’s [[Armor|armor]] to more effectively shed incoming attacks, decreasing the [[Armor|armor]]-piercing quality of any hit by 5.

### [[Ablative Hull Compartments|Ablative Hull Compartments]]

By sacrificing empty hull space in a complex system of ablative blast baffles, a capital-class ship can have a large amount of its mass shot away without actually impinging on its normal function. This grants it a +1 AC bonus and 20 extra maximum hit points.

## Fittings

### Spike [[Drive-3 upgrade|Drive-3 upgrade]]

> Power: 2 | Mass: 2 | Effect: Upgrade a spike drive to drive-2 rating

A ship can improve its standard-issue drive-1 spike drive with additional phase filters and power throughput refinements. A captain needs buy only the final grade of drive desired. He does not have to buy upgrades sequentially. Drives of rating 4 and higher are generally TL5 artifacts that cannot be built most modern worlds.

### [[Drop pod|Drop Pod]]

> Mass: 2 | Effect: Upgrade a spike drive to drive-2 rating

Armored and stealthed versions of cargo lighters, these craft are twice as fast, apply a -3 penalty to tracking and targeting skill checks, and can carry up to one hundred troops or passengers. Many are equipped with assorted [[Heavy|Heavy]] weapons to clear the landing zone, and can be treated as flight-capable gravtanks for purposes of combat. This fitting can be purchased multiple times.

### [[Armory|Armory]]

> Effect: Weapons and [[Armor|armor]] for the crew

Rather than maintaining lengthy lists of ship equipment, a captain can simply buy an [[Armory|armory]]. Ships so equipped have whatever amounts of TL4 military-grade weaponry and [[Armor|armor]] that a crew might require, and integral maintenance facilities for its upkeep. There is enough gear available to outfit the entire crew for normal use, but giving it away or losing it in use may deplete it.

### [[Ship's locker|Ship's Locker]]

> Effect: General equipment for the crew

Much like an [[Armory|armory]], this option allows a captain to lay in a general supply of equipment likely to be useful to explorers and spacemen. Any TL4 equipment on the gear list can be found in the ship’s locker in amounts commensurate with the ship’s size. A few guns and some basic [[Armor|armor]] might be included as well, but for serious armament an [[Armory|armory]] is required. There is enough gear available to outfit the entire crew for normal use, but giving it away or losing it in use may deplete the locker until it is restocked.

### [[Boarding tubes|Boarding Tubes]]

> Mass: 1 | Effect: Allows boarding of a hostile disabled ship

Armored tubes equipped with laser cutter apertures can be used to forcibly invade a hostile ship, provided the target’s engines have been disabled. Ships without [[Boarding tubes|boarding tubes]] have to send invaders across empty space to either make an assault on a doubtless heavily-guarded airlock or cut their way in through the hull with laser cutters and half an hour of [[Work|work]].

### [[Fuel scoops|Fuel Scoops]]

> Power: 2 | Mass: 2 | Effect: Ship can scoop fuel from a gas giant or star

[[Fuel scoops|Fuel scoops]] allow for the harvesting and extraction of hydrogen from gas giants or the penumbra of solar bodies. The extraction process requires four days of processing and refinement, but completely refuels the ship. Such fittings are common on explorer craft that cannot expect to find refueling stations.

### [[Advanced nav computer|Advanced Nav Computer]]

> Power: 1 | Effect: Adds +2 for traveling familiar spike courses

Forging new spike courses is too much an art to rely on computerized assistance, but an [[Advanced nav computer|advanced nav computer]] can help on well-mapped routes. When navigating an interstellar drill course with charts less than a year old, the navigator decreases drill difficulty by 2.

### Ship bay (fighter and [[Shuttle|shuttle]])

> Mass: 2 | Effect: Carrier housing for fighter and [[Shuttle|shuttle]]

These sophisticated docking bays provide all the necessary tools and support for launching a starship from the mother craft. They are rarely seen outside of dedicated capital-class carriers, but some cruisers make room to mount a fighter-class attack [[Shuttle|shuttle]]. Each bay allows room for one ship of the appropriate hull class. While the carried ship can support its own crew if necessary, most carriers fold their space wing into the mothership's crew roster. This fitting can be taken multiple times.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| **Ship Class** | Cruiser |
| **Hull Type** | Fleetcruiser |

| **AC** | 14 |

| **Crew Skill Bonus** | +2 |
| **Cost** | 17,170,000 credits |
| **Maintenance** | 858,000 credits/6mo |
| **TL** | 5 |

## Description

The archetypal warship of post-Silence humanity, the fleet cruiser is a ship-eating monster compared to its smaller brethren in the navy. Only prosperous polities can build such powerful ships, and even they sometimes find it more practical to have a flexible fleet of small craft rather than a few heavily-armed cruisers. 
The chief advantage of a fleet cruiser is in its heavily- armored hull. Only special hunter-killer ships fitted with [[Armor|armor]]-piercing weaponry have any real chance of penetrating the cruiser’s thick skin. Those weapons are almost always more bulky and power-hungry than their peer weapons, so enemy polities must usually choose between building small ships that are very effective at defeating other small ships, or building hunter-killers that can threaten cruisers but are at a disadvantage against their less specialized brethren.

## Weapons

### [[Gravcannon|Gravcannon]]

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| **Damage** | `4d6` |
| **Qualities** | AP 20 |
| **Hardpoints** | 3 |
| **Min Class** | Cruiser |
| **Cost** | 2,000,000 credits |

Using much the same principles as man-portable grav weaponry, the [[Gravcannon|gravcannon]] causes targets to fall apart in a welter of mutually-antagonistic gravitic fields.

### [[Smart Cloud|Smart Cloud]]

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| **Damage** | `3d10` |
| **Qualities** | Cloud |
| **Hardpoints** | 2 |
| **Min Class** | Cruiser |
| **Cost** | 2,000,000 credits |

A swarm of self-directed microdrones sweeps over the ship. Their integral beam weaponry is too small to damage larger ships, but they can wipe and attacking fighter wave.

### [[Multifocal Laser|Multifocal Laser]]

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| **Damage** | `1d4` |
| **Qualities** | AP 20 |
| **Hardpoints** | 0 |
| **Min Class** | Fighter |
| **Cost** | 100,000 credits |

Twinned assay and penetration lasers modulate the frequency of this beam for remarkable [[Armor|armor]] penetration. These weapons are popular choices for fighters intended for frigate or cruiser engagement.

### [[Multifocal Laser|Multifocal Laser]]

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| **Damage** | `1d4` |
| **Qualities** | AP 20 |
| **Hardpoints** | 0 |
| **Min Class** | Fighter |
| **Cost** | 100,000 credits |

Twinned assay and penetration lasers modulate the frequency of this beam for remarkable [[Armor|armor]] penetration. These weapons are popular choices for fighters intended for frigate or cruiser engagement.

## Defenses

### [[Hardened Polyceramic Overlay|Hardened Polyceramic Overlay]]

A complex glazing process can harden the surface of a ship’s [[Armor|armor]] to more effectively shed incoming attacks, decreasing the [[Armor|armor]]-piercing quality of any hit by 5.

## Fittings

### Spike [[Drive-3 upgrade|Drive-3 upgrade]]

> Power: 2 | Mass: 2 | Effect: Upgrade a spike drive to drive-2 rating

A ship can improve its standard-issue drive-1 spike drive with additional phase filters and power throughput refinements. A captain needs buy only the final grade of drive desired. He does not have to buy upgrades sequentially. Drives of rating 4 and higher are generally TL5 artifacts that cannot be built most modern worlds.

### [[Drop pod|Drop Pod]]

> Mass: 2 | Effect: Upgrade a spike drive to drive-2 rating

Armored and stealthed versions of cargo lighters, these craft are twice as fast, apply a -3 penalty to tracking and targeting skill checks, and can carry up to one hundred troops or passengers. Many are equipped with assorted [[Heavy|Heavy]] weapons to clear the landing zone, and can be treated as flight-capable gravtanks for purposes of combat. This fitting can be purchased multiple times.

### [[Armory|Armory]]

> Effect: Weapons and [[Armor|armor]] for the crew

Rather than maintaining lengthy lists of ship equipment, a captain can simply buy an [[Armory|armory]]. Ships so equipped have whatever amounts of TL4 military-grade weaponry and [[Armor|armor]] that a crew might require, and integral maintenance facilities for its upkeep. There is enough gear available to outfit the entire crew for normal use, but giving it away or losing it in use may deplete it.

### [[Ship's locker|Ship's Locker]]

> Effect: General equipment for the crew

Much like an [[Armory|armory]], this option allows a captain to lay in a general supply of equipment likely to be useful to explorers and spacemen. Any TL4 equipment on the gear list can be found in the ship’s locker in amounts commensurate with the ship’s size. A few guns and some basic [[Armor|armor]] might be included as well, but for serious armament an [[Armory|armory]] is required. There is enough gear available to outfit the entire crew for normal use, but giving it away or losing it in use may deplete the locker until it is restocked.

### [[Boarding tubes|Boarding Tubes]]

> Mass: 1 | Effect: Allows boarding of a hostile disabled ship

Armored tubes equipped with laser cutter apertures can be used to forcibly invade a hostile ship, provided the target’s engines have been disabled. Ships without [[Boarding tubes|boarding tubes]] have to send invaders across empty space to either make an assault on a doubtless heavily-guarded airlock or cut their way in through the hull with laser cutters and half an hour of [[Work|work]].

### [[Fuel scoops|Fuel Scoops]]

> Power: 2 | Mass: 2 | Effect: Ship can scoop fuel from a gas giant or star

[[Fuel scoops|Fuel scoops]] allow for the harvesting and extraction of hydrogen from gas giants or the penumbra of solar bodies. The extraction process requires four days of processing and refinement, but completely refuels the ship. Such fittings are common on explorer craft that cannot expect to find refueling stations.

### [[Advanced nav computer|Advanced Nav Computer]]

> Power: 1 | Effect: Adds +2 for traveling familiar spike courses

Forging new spike courses is too much an art to rely on computerized assistance, but an [[Advanced nav computer|advanced nav computer]] can help on well-mapped routes. When navigating an interstellar drill course with charts less than a year old, the navigator decreases drill difficulty by 2.

A mainstay of freebooting merchant-adventurers throughout human space, the standard [[Free Merchant|free merchant]] is an extremely versatile craft, capable of hauling sig- nificant amounts of cargo to neighboring systems while requiring very few hands to operate it. Only one crew member is needed for in-system flight, though spike drills require three for normal margins of safety.
The standard [[Free Merchant|free merchant]] is not a warship, but its [[Sandthrower|sandthrower]] is enough to discourage pirate shuttles and the other small or fragile craft that wreckers or primitive worlds tend to favor. ## Description

Patrol boats are often the largest ships fielded by poor or backward frontier worlds that lack the shipyard fa- cilities or available resources to build bigger military craft. Even so, the ability to field two patrol boats for the yearly maintenance cost of one [[Corvette|corvette]] often ap- peals even to richer worlds that need more coverage than their available craft can provide. 
Patrol boats are the smallest independent warships fielded by most navies, as fighters are not normally considered capable of extended independent opera- tion. They have considerable spike drive reach and are faster in-system than most of their potential targets. While their single mounted gun is vulnerable to being disabled by expert enemy gunners, the relatively thick [[Armor|armor]] of the ship and skilled damage control crew can mitigate that danger. A few patrol boats replace their [[Survey sensor array|survey sensor array]] with a [[Sandthrower|sandthrower]] to up-gun the ship, but most prefer the additional edge in scanning potential [[Smugglers|smugglers]].

## Description

This craft is a conventional civilian shuttle, albeit one with a spike drive sufficient to get it to a neighboring system and enough passenger space to make it a minimally- acceptable transport for brave VIPs and light cargo. If used as an inter-system transport, however, at least three crew will be needed to safely navigate a drill. While cheap and flexible, the shuttle is entirely unarmed and acutely vulnerable to piracy or hostile warships. In such cases the pilot’s only recourse is to surrender or hope the small craft’s nimble maneuver drives can keep it away from the attacker long enough to get to safety.

## Fittings

### [[Atmospheric configuration|Atmospheric Configuration]]

> Mass: 1 | Effect: Can land: frigates and fighters only.

This fitting must be put in place when the ship is built, and cannot be installed on cruiser-class or larger ships. A ship designed for atmospheric flight can land on most solid or aqueous surfaces.

### [[Extended life support|Extended life support]]

> Power: 1 | Mass: 1 | Effect: Can land: frigates and fighters only.

The ship can be designed to accommodate a larger number of crew or passengers. [[Extended life support|Extended life support]] can be fitted multiple times; each time, the maximum crew rating of the ship increases by 100% of its normal maximum. Thus, a [[Free Merchant|free merchant]] who installs this twice can have a maximum complement of 18 people.

This particular model is equipped with a [[Reaper Battery|reaper battery]] for dealing with small, lightly-armored civilian ships. “[[Bomber|Bomber]]”-type fighters usually replace this with a [[Fractal Impact Charge|fractal impact charge]] to threaten larger warships, while fighters built to dogfight their peers favor fitting a [[Multifocal Laser|multifocal laser]].

name: Connect
body: Find people who can be helpful to your purposes and get them to cooperate with you. Roll it to make useful connections with others, find people you [[Know|know]], [[Know|know]] where to get illicit goods and services, and be familiar with foreign cultures and languages. You can use it in place of [[Talk|Talk]] for persuading people you find via this skill.

name: Exert
body: Apply trained speed, strength, or stamina in some feat of physical exertion. Roll it to run, jump, [[Lift|lift]], swim, climb, throw, and so forth. You can use it as a combat skill when throwing things, though it doesn’t qualify as a combat skill for other ends.

name: Fix (SWNAWNCWN) Craft (WWN)
body:
Create and repair devices both simple and complex. How complex will depend on your character’s background; a lostworlder blacksmith is going to need some study time before he’s ready to fix that broken fusion reactor, though he can do it eventually. Roll it to fix things, build things, and identify what something is supposed to do.

-

Craft or repair goods and technology appropriate to the PC’s background and society. The Craft skill can be used for a wide range of artisan pursuits, though a GM is within their rights to keep the PC from building complex things that are too far away from their past background and experience.

name: Heal
body: Employ medical and psychological treatment for the injured or disturbed. Roll it to cure diseases, stabilize the critically injured, treat psychological disorders, or diagnose illnesses.

name: Know
body: Know facts about academic or scientific fields. Roll it to understand planetary ecologies, remember relevant history, solve science mysteries, and know the basic facts about rare or esoteric topics.

name: Lead
body: Convince others to also do whatever it is you’re trying to do. [[Talk|Talk]] might persuade them that following you is smart, but Lead can make them do it even when they think it’s a bad idea. Roll it to lead troops in combat, convince others to follow you, or maintain morale and discipline.

name: Magic (WWN)
body: Cast or analyze magic and [[Know|know]] things about famous mages or notable magical events. Classes that can’t cast spells obtain only intellectual and scholarly benefits from this skill.

name: Metapsionics
body: Master [[Powers|powers]] that nullify, boost, and shape the use of other psychic abilities.

name: Notice
body: Spot anomalies or interesting facts about your environment. Roll it for searching places, detecting ambushes, spotting things, and reading the emotional state of other people.

name: Perform
body: Exhibit some performative skill. Roll it to dance, sing, orate, act, or otherwise put on a convincing or emotionally moving performance.

name: Pilot (SWNAWNCWN) Sail (WWN)
body:
Use this skill to pilot vehicles or ride beasts. Roll it to fly spaceships, drive vehicles, ride animals, or tend to basic vehicle repair. This skill doesn’t help you with things entirely outside the scope of your background or experience, though with some practice a PC can expand their expertise.

-

Sail or repair a ship, build small craft, navigate by the stars, read sea weather, manage sailors, and otherwise conduct the business of a professional mariner. This skill may apply to more esoteric means of vehicular travel in some societies

name: Pray (WWN)
body: [[Perform|Perform]] the clerical rites of your religion, and be familiar with the gods, demons, and taboos of major and minor faiths, and identify iconography and persons of religious importance. Pray also helps you [[Know|know]] the state of local faiths and the important persons in their hierarchies

name: Precognition
body: Master the ability to sense future events and control probability.

name: Program (SWNCWNAWN)
body: Operating or hacking computing and [[Communications|communications]] hardware. Roll it to program or hack computers, control computer-operated hardware, operate [[Communications|communications]] tech, or decrypt things.

name: Punch
body: Use it as a combat skill when fighting unarmed. If your PC means to make a habit of this rather than as a recourse of desperation, you should take the [[Unarmed Combatant|Unarmed Combatant]] focus described later.

name: Ride (WWN) Drive (CWNSWNAWN)
body: Ride an animal, drive a cart or carriage, or otherwise deal with land transportation. This skill also includes competence at mount care and tending, basic cart or carriage repair, judging good horseflesh, and other [[Skills|skills]] appropriate to a beast-rider of whatever society the PC comes from.

name: Shoot
body: Use it as a combat skill when using [[Ranged|ranged]] weaponry, whether hurled rocks, bows, laser pistols, combat rifles, or ship’s gunnery.

name: Sneak
body: Move without drawing [[Notice|notice]]. Roll it for [[Stealth|stealth]], disguise, infiltration, manual legerdemain, pickpocketing, and the defeat of security measures.

name: Stab
body: Use it as a combat skill when wielding [[Melee|melee]] weapons, whether primitive or complex.

name: Survive
body: Obtain the basics of food, water, and shelter in hostile environments, along with avoiding their natural perils. Roll it to handle animals, navigate difficult terrain, scrounge urban resources, make basic tools, and avoid wild beasts or gangs.

name: Talk
body: Convince other people of the facts you want them to believe. What they do with that conviction may not be completely predictable. Roll it to persuade, charm, or deceive others in conversation.

name: Telekinesis
body: Master the remote control of kinetic energy to move objects and fabricate force constructs.

name: Telepath
body: Master the reading and influencing of other sapient minds.

name: Teleportation
body: Master the arts of physical translocation of yourself and allies.

name: Trade
body: Find what you need on the market and sell what you have. Roll it to sell or buy things, figure out where to purchase hard-to-get or illicit goods, deal with customs agents, or run a business.

name: Work
body: This is a catch-all skill for professions not represented by other [[Skills|skills]]. Roll it to work at a particular profession, art, or [[Trade|trade]]

## Description

The fixed-wing aircraft used on planets too primitive to have developed gravitic technology. Faster and simpler to maintain than comparable helicopters, they can also carry more cargo on most worlds. The need for clear, hard terrain for landing and take-off limits their use on some rugged worlds. This model represents a small personal jet.

## Description

Rugged vehicles, either wheeled or tracked, and driven by type B power cells or locally-available biofuels. While they can't navigate rough terrain as easily as a grav vehicle, they're designed to take a tremendous amount of punishment before breaking down and support repairs using basic tools and frontier expedients.

body:
| Stat | Value |

| **HP** | 25 |
| **Crew** | 5 |
| **Tonnage** | 10 |
| **TL** | 4 |
| **Weapon Mounts** | 1 |

## Description

The standard personal vehicle of most TL4 worlds, though most lower-class citizens rely on public transport in urban areas. Most advanced worlds have planetary transit grids that allow occupants to simply code in a destination and let the car take them there. Where infrastructure or local conditions preclude that convenience, manual controls and Pilot skill can be used.

| **Tonnage** | 50 |
| **TL** | 4 |
| **Weapon Mounts** | 2 |

## Description

The usual long-distance transport on most TL4 worlds. Large enough to support the gravitics required for true flight, a few models can even reach low orbit. All can hover and climb with typical gravitic ease. This particular gravflyer is a small craft suitable for an affluent owner and their family.

name: Gravtank
body:
| Stat | Value |

| **HP** | 50 |
| **Crew** | 3 |
| **Tonnage** | 50 |
| **TL** | 5 |
| **Weapon Mounts** | 6 |

## Description

The bulk of a prosperous TL4 world's armored forces. Private ownership is strictly forbidden on most worlds, but "export models" often can be acquired for transport offworld. Gravtanks have armor heavy enough to ignore all damage from conventional small arms, and can only be harmed by Heavy weapons or properly-placed demolitions charges — immune to anything short of TL4 Heavy weapons, while less sophisticated tanks are immune to anything below TL3 Heavy ordnance. Equipped with advanced targeting systems, so all of its weapons can be targeted and fired by a single gunner.

## Description

Groundcars are the TL3 analogs of the vehicles commonly in use on 21st-century Earth, allowing for some minor variations in electronics and capabilities. Primitive buggies of various kinds are found even on higher-tech worlds, thanks to their ease of construction and maintenance compared to the delicate gravitics of more modern vehicles.

Used on TL3 worlds where a lack of airfields or treacherous local terrain prohibits the use of fixed-wing craft. Their ability to hover over an area or drop onto a tightly-constrained landing zone makes them particular favorites of quick-response military forces and groups in need of fast fire support. This model represents a medium-weight civilian craft that might be repurposed by militia or adventurers.

name: Ashvale Coalition
body:
## Overview

A breakaway warlord alliance holding the Ashvale highlands of Kestrel II, built from a Council militia regiment that walked away when New Kestrel City cut highland funding to pay for Port Kestrel's defenses. Fights out of a fortress built into a Mandate-era bunker and has no intention of ever bending the knee to the Council again.

## Faction Stats

| Stat      | Value          |
| --------- | -------------- |
| Force     | 6              |
| Cunning   | 2              |
| Wealth    | 4              |
| HP        | 16             |
| FacCreds  | 4              |
| XP        | 2              |
| Homeworld | [[Kestrel II]] |
| Tags      | Warlike        |

## Goal

- Planetary Seizure — depose the Kestrel Corporate Council and become the legitimate government of Kestrel II.

## Assets

- [[Guerrilla Populace]] — highland partisans and irregulars loyal to Ashvale
- [[Zealots]] — hardened veterans of the original breakaway regiment, willing to fight to the death

## Leadership & Members

- **Warlord** — [[Warlord Rurik Ashvale]], former Council militia commander
- **Infiltrator** — [[Corporal Nyssa Thorne]], embedded among Council dockworkers at the Anchorage on [[Vesper Hollow]]
- A regiment's worth of highland fighters and their families, genuinely convinced they're fighting for Ashvale's survival

## Territory & Holdings

- Ashvale Hold (fortified seat of power, built into a Mandate-era bunker)
- The Ashvale highlands continent, contested at the edges
- [[Ashvale's Answer]] — a captured Council gravtank, the Coalition's single most feared asset on the ground
- No fixed holdings at [[Vesper System]], but a single embedded agent watching the Council's back-channel supply relay there

## Relationships & Rivals

- At war with the [[Kestrel Corporate Council]], led by [[Governor Lian Osk]]
- Buys weapons from the [[Red Veil Cartel]] via [[Captain Vashti Kael]], though Ashvale doesn't fully trust them

| Tags      | Planetary Government     |

## Goal

- Destroy the Foe (Ashvale Coalition) — grind down the Coalition's assets until it can no longer hold Ashvale Hold, ideally with the help of outside mercenaries the Council can deny hiring if it goes badly.

## Assets

- [[Monopoly]] — tacit stranglehold on Port Kestrel's tariffs and trade licenses
- [[Militia Unit]] — New Kestrel City militia, spread thin defending Meridian's cities

## Leadership & Members

- **Governor** — [[Governor Lian Osk]], career administrator holding the Council together with concessions and backroom deals
- **Station-Chief** — [[Warden Petra Voss]], runs a discreet listening post and supply relay at the Anchorage on [[Vesper Hollow]]
- Council formalwear bureaucracy, increasingly hollowed out by the war effort

## Territory & Holdings

- New Kestrel City (capital, orbital elevator terminus)
- Dawnreach (secondary port city, shipbuilding)
- Nominal claim over all of Meridian continent
- A small listening post and supply relay at the Anchorage on [[Vesper Hollow]], [[Vesper System]] — a back channel that bypasses Coalition-contested space

## Relationships & Rivals

- At war with the [[Ashvale Coalition]], led by [[Warlord Rurik Ashvale]]
- Tolerates the [[Kestrel Free Traders Association]] to keep Port Kestrel functioning
- Osk maintains a secret backchannel to the [[Mandate Remnant Surveyors]], undisclosed to the rest of the Council

name: Kestrel Free Traders Association
body:
## Overview

A neutral merchant guild trying to keep Port Kestrel open to both sides of the Kestrel II civil war. One of the few organizations both the Council and the Ashvale Coalition still let dock unmolested, and determined to keep it that way.

## Faction Stats

| Stat      | Value              |
| --------- | ------------------ |
| Force     | 1                  |
| Cunning   | 3                  |
| Wealth    | 4                  |
| HP        | 12                 |
| FacCreds  | 4                  |
| XP        | 1                  |
| Homeworld | [[Kestrel II]]     |
| Tags      | Exchange Consulate |

## Goal

- Peaceable Kingdom — stay out of the war entirely; no Attack actions, no picking sides.

## Assets

- [[Freighter Contract]] — links with heavy shipping spacers, keeps cargo and refugees moving
- [[Franchise]] — deniable local licensing arrangements that keep the Association's books flexible

## Leadership & Members

- **Captain (Kestrel Drift)** — Dessa Vray, former Council customs officer who quit rather than pick a side
- **Captain (Wayward Cairn)** — [[Captain Joss Merrin]], runs the alternate corridor through [[Vesper Hollow]] now that the direct Kestrel run has grown dangerous
- A loose guild of independent captains and dockworkers displaced by the fighting

## Territory & Holdings

- Port Kestrel (shared orbital free port)
- No ground holdings — deliberately avoids planetside entanglement
- A regular trade circuit through the Anchorage on [[Vesper Hollow]], [[Vesper System]], run by the [[Wayward Cairn]]

## Relationships & Rivals

- Tolerated by both the [[Kestrel Corporate Council]] and the [[Ashvale Coalition]] as long as it stays neutral
- The [[Red Veil Cartel]] has threatened to intercept an Association run, testing that neutrality

name: Mandate Remnant Surveyors
body:
## Overview

A pretech survey and archival organization cataloging Mandate-era ruins and infrastructure across the sector. Their presence in Kestrel is no accident — they're quietly investigating the orbital elevator ruins on Kestrel II and the theft of one of their own patrol craft, now sailing under a different name.

## Faction Stats

| Stat      | Value            |
| --------- | ---------------- |
| Force     | 1                |
| Cunning   | 4                |
| Wealth    | 3                |
| HP        | 12               |
| FacCreds  | 3                |
| XP        | 1                |
| Homeworld | (itinerant)      |
| Tags      | Perimeter Agency |

## Goal

- Expand Influence — get a quiet foothold on Kestrel III's moons to study the pretech cache before either local faction weaponizes it; the Vesper Array investigation has already yielded a working model of what a failing pretech site looks like up close.

## Assets

- [[Surveyors]] — resource and ruin survey crews, currently cataloging the Kestrel elevator anchors and the failing array in Vesper System
- [[Informers]] — a thin but watchful network keeping tabs on who's moving what through the system

## Leadership & Members

- **Archivist** — Archivist Renn Toll, meticulous field agent, captain of the [[Pale Cartographer]]
- **Field Archivist** — [[Field Archivist Sela Brint]], stationed at [[Vesper's Shroud]] investigating the failing Mandate relay array behind Vesper Reach's instability
- Researchers and technicians, unarmed but well-connected

## Territory & Holdings

- No fixed base in-system; operates out of the [[Pale Cartographer]]
- Maintains archives elsewhere in the sector (old Mandate-era system charts, including data on Kestrel III's moons)
- An active field investigation at the Vesper Array on [[Vesper's Shroud]], [[Vesper System]]

## Relationships & Rivals

- Maintains a quiet backchannel to [[Governor Lian Osk]] and the [[Kestrel Corporate Council]], hoping to trade access to Mandate ruins for protection
- Holds a standing bounty against [[Captain Vashti Kael]] and the [[Red Veil Cartel]] for the theft of the [[Nightshade Vow]]

name: Red Veil Cartel
body:
## Overview

Smugglers exploiting the Kestrel II civil war to move weapons and spike drive components under cover of the Shattered Belt's mining traffic. Loyal to neither the Council nor the Coalition — only to the profit margin the war keeps generating.

## Faction Stats

| Stat      | Value                  |
| --------- | ---------------------- |
| Force     | 2                      |
| Cunning   | 5                      |
| Wealth    | 4                      |
| HP        | 15                     |
| FacCreds  | 5                      |
| XP        | 2                      |
| Homeworld | [[The Shattered Belt]] |
| Tags      | Secretive              |

## Goal

- Expand Influence — extend the smuggling network into Kestrel III's moons, where the weapons Kael is running actually originate; the new Driftfield operation at Vesper System is the first concrete step.

## Assets

- [[Smugglers]] — crews skilled at slipping personnel and cargo past customs
- [[Covert Shipping]] — quiet interstellar transport for the Cartel's contraband runs

## Leadership & Members

- **Captain** — [[Captain Vashti Kael]], the Cartel's point woman for the Kestrel run, captain of the [[Nightshade Vow]]
- **Enforcer** — [[Enforcer Dashiell Corr]], runs Red Veil's salvage and smuggling operation out of [[The Driftfield]], captain of the [[Widow's Toll]]
- Ex-Mandate military washouts loyal to Kael personally rather than the Cartel itself

## Territory & Holdings

- Operates out of [[The Shattered Belt]], disguised among the mining traffic — no fixed base or headquarters, deliberately kept mobile
- A forward salvage and smuggling operation in [[The Driftfield]], [[Vesper System]], fencing goods through the Anchorage on [[Vesper Hollow]]

## Relationships & Rivals

- Runs weapons to [[Warlord Rurik Ashvale]] and the [[Ashvale Coalition]], though Kael would sell to the [[Kestrel Corporate Council]] just as readily for the right price
- The Cartel's only reliable source of spare parts and ammunition for [[Ashvale's Answer]], the Coalition's captured Council gravtank
- Stole the [[Nightshade Vow]] from the [[Mandate Remnant Surveyors]], who now have a bounty out on Kael

name: Captain Joss Merrin
body:
## Overview

Merrin started running the Vesper Reach corridor when the direct routes into Kestrel got too dangerous for an unarmed free trader to risk. Now the Wayward Cairn's regular circuit has made Merrin one of the few people who understands just how many factions are quietly using Vesper Hollow as a back door.

## Appearance & Personality

- Easygoing and talkative, the kind of captain who remembers everyone's name and asks after their family
- Fiercely protective of the Association's neutrality, having seen firsthand what happens to traders who pick a side
- Better informed about what's really going on in Vesper System than almost anyone gives credit for

## Stats & Combat

| Stat      | Value            |
| --------- | ------------------ |
| Statblock | [[Peaceful Human]]   |
| HD        | 1                      |
| AC        | 10                        |
| Attack    | +0                           |
| Saves     | 15                               |
| Morale    | 6                                    |

## Relationships & Factions

- Captains the [[Wayward Cairn]] for the [[Kestrel Free Traders Association]], running the alternate corridor through [[Vesper Hollow]]
- On cordial terms with [[Warden Petra Voss]] and [[Field Archivist Sela Brint]]; keeps a careful, professional distance from [[Enforcer Dashiell Corr]]
- Trades information almost as often as cargo — Merrin knows things worth more than the manifest suggests

name: Captain Vashti Kael
body:
## Overview

Captain of the Nightshade Vow and the Red Veil Cartel's point woman for the Kestrel run, Kael has made a fortune keeping both sides of the Kestrel II civil war armed and fighting. She's not loyal to either faction — only to the profit margin the war keeps generating.

## Appearance & Personality

- Former Mandate Remnant Surveyors navigator, still wears a modified Surveyor flight jacket with the insignia cut off
- Cold and businesslike; treats every negotiation like a transaction, including threats
- Keeps her crew fiercely loyal through generous cuts and brutal discipline

## Stats & Combat

| Stat      | Value         |
| --------- | ------------- |
| Statblock | [[Gang Boss]] |
| HD        | 3             |
| AC        | 14            |
| Attack    | +4            |
| Saves     | 14            |
| Morale    | 9             |

## Relationships & Factions

- Runs weapons for the Red Veil Cartel into the Kestrel II civil war
- Sells to [[Warlord Rurik Ashvale]] and the Ashvale Coalition, though she'd sell to the Council just as readily for the right price
- Stole the [[Nightshade Vow]] from the Mandate Remnant Surveyors, who now have a bounty on her

name: Corporal Nyssa Thorne
body:
## Overview

Sent through the Reach months ago posing as a Meridian refugee, Thorne has worked her way into the Anchorage's dockworker crews and now has better visibility into the Council's supply relay than anyone in Ashvale Hold expected. She reports back irregularly, whenever a trustworthy courier passes through.

## Appearance & Personality

- Unremarkable by design — plain, quiet, forgettable in a room full of louder refugees
- Genuinely believes in the Coalition's cause, but has grown wary of how long she's been out of contact with Ashvale Hold
- Has started making her own calls about what to report and what to sit on, which would trouble her superiors if they knew

## Stats & Combat

| Stat      | Value             |
| --------- | ------------------- |
| Statblock | [[Military Soldier]]  |
| HD        | 1                       |
| AC        | 16                         |
| Attack    | +1                            |
| Saves     | 15                                |
| Morale    | 9                                     |

## Relationships & Factions

- Embedded at the Anchorage on [[Vesper Hollow]], reporting intelligence back to [[Warlord Rurik Ashvale]]
- Has infiltrated [[Warden Petra Voss]]'s dockworker crews without detection
- Avoids [[Enforcer Dashiell Corr]]'s Red Veil operation, not trusting the Cartel any more than her Warlord does

name: Enforcer Dashiell Corr

frontmatter.name: Enforcer Dashiell Corr
frontmatter.role: Red Veil Cartel Enforcer (Driftfield Salvage Boss)

body:
## Overview

"Dash" Corr runs Red Veil's Driftfield operation on Vashti Kael's authority — salvage on the surface, smuggling underneath. Ex-Mandate military like most of Kael's inner circle, Corr treats the wreck field like a personal fiefdom and has little patience for independent scavengers who don't take the hint to move on.

## Appearance & Personality

- Broad-shouldered and scarred, wears salvaged void armor plating like a badge of rank
- Blunt and businesslike, more comfortable giving orders than negotiating
- Fiercely loyal to Kael personally, less so to the Cartel as an institution

## Stats & Combat

| Stat      | Value           |
| --------- | ----------------- |
| Statblock | [[Military Elite]]  |
| HD        | 3                     |
| AC        | 16                        |
| Attack    | +4                            |
| Saves     | 14                                |
| Morale    | 10                                    |

## Relationships & Factions

- Runs [[Red Veil Cartel]] salvage and smuggling operations out of [[The Driftfield]], captaining the [[Widow's Toll]]
- Reports to [[Captain Vashti Kael]] and fences goods through the Anchorage on [[Vesper Hollow]]
- Keeps a wary, unspoken truce with [[Warden Petra Voss]]'s Council listening post — neither wants a fight neither can afford

name: Field Archivist Sela Brint
body:
## Overview

Dispatched by Archivist Renn Toll to investigate why Vesper Reach has grown so unreliable, Brint found her answer within weeks: a dying Mandate relay array anchored to one of Vesper's Shroud's moons, its systems failing after centuries without maintenance. What she's found since has raised more questions than it answered.

## Appearance & Personality

- Methodical to the point of obsession, rarely without a data slate recording every reading
- More at ease around old Mandate hardware than around people
- Growing increasingly uneasy about how much of the array's original purpose remains unclear

## Stats & Combat

| Stat      | Value           |
| --------- | ----------------- |
| Statblock | [[Normal Human]]     |
| HD        | 1                       |
| AC        | 10                          |
| Attack    | +0                              |
| Saves     | 15                                  |
| Morale    | 6                                       |

## Relationships & Factions

- Reports to Archivist Renn Toll aboard the [[Pale Cartographer]] on behalf of the [[Mandate Remnant Surveyors]]
- Stationed near the Vesper Array on [[Vesper's Shroud]], passing through [[Vesper Hollow]] for supplies and courier contact
- Wary of [[Enforcer Dashiell Corr]]'s salvage crews working too close to what may be pieces of the array itself

name: Governor Lian Osk
body:
## Overview

The nominal head of the Kestrel Corporate Council, Osk inherited a losing war and a crumbling mandate. She is not a soldier or a warlord — she's a career administrator trying to hold a fracturing planetary government together with trade concessions, promises, and increasingly desperate backroom deals.

## Appearance & Personality

- Sharp, exhausted, and precise; dresses in Council formalwear even during air raids
- Pragmatic to a fault — will deal with pirates, mercenaries, or worse if it keeps New Kestrel City standing
- Privately doubts the Council can win, but won't say so publicly

## Stats & Combat

| Stat      | Value            |
| --------- | ---------------- |
| Statblock | [[Normal Human]] |
| HD        | 1                |
| AC        | 10               |
| Attack    | +0               |
| Saves     | 15               |
| Morale    | 6                |

## Relationships & Factions

- Head of the Kestrel Corporate Council, based in New Kestrel City
- At war with the Ashvale Coalition, led by [[Warlord Rurik Ashvale]]
- Maintains a secret backchannel to the Mandate Remnant Surveyors

name: Warden Petra Voss
body:
## Overview

Nominally just a customs officer, Voss actually runs the Council's entire back-channel supply relay through the Anchorage — a lifeline to New Kestrel City that doesn't have to run past the Ashvale Coalition's lines. She reports directly to Governor Osk and to almost nobody else, which suits her fine.

## Appearance & Personality

- Precise and unflappable, with a customs officer's gift for making paperwork sound like small talk
- Runs the listening post on a shoestring and knows it; resents Council command for expecting more than they fund
- Quietly contemptuous of the other factions using the Anchorage, but pragmatic enough to work around them rather than against them

## Stats & Combat

| Stat      | Value                  |
| --------- | ------------------------ |
| Statblock | [[Skilled Professional]] |
| HD        | 1                          |
| AC        | 10                           |
| Attack    | +0                             |
| Saves     | 15                                |
| Morale    | 6                                    |

## Relationships & Factions

- Runs the Council's listening post and supply relay at the Anchorage on [[Vesper Hollow]], reporting to [[Governor Lian Osk]]
- Unaware that [[Corporal Nyssa Thorne]] is an Ashvale plant embedded among her own dockworkers
- Maintains a wary, transactional peace with [[Enforcer Dashiell Corr]]'s Red Veil operation rather than risk a confrontation she can't win

name: Warlord Rurik Ashvale
body:
## Overview

A former Council militia commander who broke away with half his regiment when the Council cut Ashvale highlands funding to pay for Port Kestrel's defenses. Now he leads the Coalition from a fortress built into a Mandate-era bunker, and he has no intention of ever bending the knee to New Kestrel City again.

## Appearance & Personality

- Built like the soldier he still is; wears mismatched Council-surplus armor as a trophy
- Charismatic to his own people, ruthless to anyone he considers an occupier
- Genuinely believes he's fighting for Ashvale's survival, not just his own power

## Stats & Combat

| Stat      | Value              |
| --------- | ------------------ |
| Statblock | [[Warrior Tyrant]] |
| HD        | 8                  |
| AC        | 20                 |
| Attack    | +10                |
| Saves     | 11                 |
| Morale    | 11                 |

## Relationships & Factions

- Commands the Ashvale Coalition from Ashvale Hold
- At war with [[Governor Lian Osk]] and the Kestrel Corporate Council
- Buys weapons from the Red Veil Cartel, run by [[Captain Vashti Kael]], though he doesn't fully trust them

name: Hydra Sector
body:
## Overview

A frontier sector on the ragged edge of settled space, cut off from Old Earth like every other fragment of the Mandate's fallen web. Most of what's currently mapped clusters around Kestrel System, a busy trade crossroads at the junction of three jump routes, with a second foothold now established at Vesper System via the once-unreliable Vesper Reach. The rest of the sector remains unexplored from the party's perspective.

## Sector Map

| System  | Coordinates | Primary World      | Tags                                | Link                |
| ------- | ----------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------------- |
| Kestrel | 0507        | [[Kestrel II]]      | Trade Hub, Frontier, Pirate Activity  | [[Kestrel System]]   |
| Vesper  | 0303        | [[Vesper Hollow]]   | Frontier, Mandate Ruins, Unstable Jump Lane | [[Vesper System]]    |

## Polities & Governments

- No faction currently holds territory beyond a single system — the [[Kestrel Corporate Council]] and [[Ashvale Coalition]] are both confined to contesting Kestrel II itself, not yet a sector-spanning polity
- [[Red Veil Cartel]], [[Kestrel Free Traders Association]], and the [[Mandate Remnant Surveyors]] all operate across system lines but hold no fixed territory in the sector; all five now have at least a small foothold at Vesper System as well

## Trade Routes & Jump Lanes

- [[Ashen Gate]] — 6 days from Kestrel, unexplored beyond the jump point
- [[Vesper Reach]] — 4 days from Kestrel; now confirmed to reach [[Vesper System]], though the route's instability has only gotten worse
- [[Red Talon]] — 9 days from Kestrel, unexplored beyond the jump point

## Frontier & Unknowns

- Most of the sector outside Kestrel's immediate neighborhood is still unmapped
- No confirmed border jump routes into neighboring sectors yet
- The Silent Span, a second jump route out of Vesper System, remains unexplored beyond its jump point

name: Kestrel Drift
body:
## Overview

A battered but reliable free merchant that shuttles cargo and refugees between Port Kestrel and the surface, one of the few vessels both the Council and the Ashvale Coalition still let dock unmolested. Its crew has made a point of staying scrupulously neutral in the civil war raging below.

## Stats

| Stat        | Value             |
| ----------- | ----------------- |
| Hull Type   | [[Free Merchant]] |
| HP          | 20                |
| AC          | 14                |
| Armor       | 2                 |
| Speed       | 3                 |
| Spike Drive | Drive-1           |
| Crew        | 1/6               |
| TL          | 5                 |

## Crew

- **Captain** — Dessa Vray, a former Council customs officer who quit rather than pick a side
- Six crew, mostly Meridian dockworkers displaced by the fighting

## Cargo & Notable Gear

- Mixed cargo: medical supplies, refined ore, and refugees running below manifest
- A hidden compartment for smuggling non-combatants past both factions' checkpoints

## History

- Formerly a Council customs cutter before being decommissioned and sold to the Free Traders Association
- Has ferried wounded from Ashvale Hold to New Kestrel City's hospitals on at least two occasions, drawing suspicion from Council hardliners

name: Nightshade Vow
body:
## Overview

A stripped-down corvette running dark paint and a spoofed transponder, the Nightshade Vow is the Red Veil Cartel's favored ship for running weapons and spike drive components into the Shattered Belt under cover of the mining traffic. Fast, armored, and willing to fight its way out of trouble.

## Stats

| Stat        | Value        |
| ----------- | ------------ |
| Hull Type   | [[Corvette]] |
| HP          | 40           |
| AC          | 13           |
| Armor       | 10           |
| Speed       | 2            |
| Spike Drive | Drive-2      |
| Crew        | 6            |
| TL          | 5            |

## Crew

- **Captain** — [[Captain Vashti Kael]]
- Six-person crew, mostly ex-Mandate military washouts loyal to Kael personally

## Cargo & Notable Gear

- Falsified cargo manifests disguising weapon crates as mining equipment
- A cache of military-grade spike drive components bound for the Ashvale Coalition

## History

- Formerly a Mandate Remnant Surveyors patrol craft, stolen by Kael's crew during a refueling stop years ago
- Has slipped past Port Kestrel customs at least a dozen times using forged Free Traders Association credentials

name: Pale Cartographer
body:
## Overview

A converted free merchant repurposed as a survey vessel, the Pale Cartographer catalogs pretech ruins and Mandate-era infrastructure across the sector. Its presence in Kestrel is no accident — the Surveyors are quietly investigating both the orbital elevator ruins on Kestrel II and the theft of one of their own patrol craft, now sailing under a different name.

## Stats

| Stat        | Value             |
| ----------- | ----------------- |
| Hull Type   | [[Free Merchant]] |
| HP          | 20                |
| AC          | 14                |
| Armor       | 2                 |
| Speed       | 3                 |
| Spike Drive | Drive-1           |
| Crew        | 5                 |
| TL          | 5                 |

## Crew

- **Captain** — Archivist Renn Toll, a meticulous Surveyor field agent
- Five researchers and technicians, unarmed but well-connected

## Cargo & Notable Gear

- Survey drones and deep-scan sensor arrays
- Sealed archive of Mandate-era system charts, including old data on Kestrel III's moons

## History

- Dispatched to Kestrel System to assess the civil war's threat to pretech sites in the region
- Has quietly reached out to Governor Osk's administration for access and protection

name: Wayward Cairn
body:
## Overview

A free merchant running the Vesper Reach corridor on a steady loop, carrying cargo, mail, and the occasional passenger between Vesper Hollow and Port Kestrel. Merrin keeps it scrupulously legal, which has made the Cairn one of the few ships every faction in Vesper System trusts enough to leave alone.

## Stats

| Stat        | Value             |
| ----------- | ----------------- |
| Hull Type   | [[Free Merchant]] |
| HP          | 20                |
| AC          | 14                |
| Armor       | 2                 |
| Speed       | 3                 |
| Spike Drive | Drive-1           |
| Crew        | 1/5               |
| TL          | 5                 |

## Crew

- **Captain** — [[Captain Joss Merrin]]
- Four crew, mostly veterans of the Kestrel-Vesper run who know the Reach's quirks better than most pilots

## Cargo & Notable Gear

- General cargo: mail, spare parts, medical supplies, and the occasional refugee moving quietly between systems
- A well-worn set of charts noting where Vesper Reach's instability tends to bite hardest

## History

- Purchased secondhand by the Free Traders Association specifically to open the Vesper corridor once the direct Kestrel routes grew too dangerous
- Has never missed a scheduled run, a point of quiet pride for its crew

name: Widow's Toll
body:
## Overview

A former frontier-navy patrol boat, stripped of its markings and repainted matte black, the Widow's Toll is Red Veil's enforcement arm in the Driftfield — fast enough to run down scavengers who won't take a hint, armored enough to shrug off the debris field's hazards.

## Stats

| Stat        | Value          |
| ----------- | -------------- |
| Hull Type   | [[Patrol Boat]] |
| HP          | 25             |
| AC          | 14             |
| Armor       | 5              |
| Speed       | 4              |
| Spike Drive | Drive-2        |
| Crew        | 8              |
| TL          | 5              |

## Crew

- **Captain** — [[Enforcer Dashiell Corr]]
- Eight crew, mostly ex-military muscle brought in to enforce Red Veil's claim over the Driftfield's best salvage

## Cargo & Notable Gear

- Salvaged hull plate and scavenged components awaiting transfer to the Anchorage's black market
- A locked hold nobody outside Corr's inner circle has been allowed to inspect

## History

- Acquired by the Cartel through channels Corr has never fully explained, even to Kael
- Has run off at least three independent scavenger crews from claims Corr wanted for Red Veil

name: SWN-session-context
body:
This file records the primary game rule and universe sources for Stars Without Number in this workspace.

## Primary sources

- `StarsWithoutNumberRevised-FreeEdition.txt`
  - The main rules text for the free edition in this repo.
  - Contains core rules, character creation, psionics, systems, equipment, ships, sector creation, and more.

- `Compendium/`
  - A collection of Markdown notes for rules, items, cyberware, creatures, armor, equipment, ships, and more.
  - Key subfolders include:
    - `Armor/`
    - `Creatures/`
    - `Cyberware/`
    - `Equipment/`
    - `Faction Assets/`
    - `Features & Foci/`
    - `NPCs/`
    - `Psychic Powers/`
    - `Robots/`
    - `Ship Defenses/`
    - `Ship Fittings/`
    - `Ship Weapons/`
    - `Ships/`
    - `Skills/`
    - `Vehicles/`
    - `Weapons/`

## How to use this file

1. When starting a new session, open `SWN-session-context.md` first.
2. Ask the assistant to load or refresh context from the listed files.
3. If you want a deeper context load, include specific directories or documents to read.

## Recommended action

- Load `StarsWithoutNumberRevised-FreeEdition.txt` for the core game rules.
- Load the `Compendium/` folder for the edited and curated rule/object notes.

## Notes

- The assistant does not automatically load these files on session start.
- This file is a workspace-visible reference to make manual context loading faster.

name: Kestrel System
body:
## Overview

A busy frontier system on the edge of settled space. Kestrel serves as a natural crossroads between three jump routes and has become a rough trading hub.

## Stellar Characteristics

| Star            | Type | Notes                       |
| --------------- | ---- | --------------------------- |
| Kestrel Primary | G2V  | Stable yellow star          |
| Kestrel B       | M4V  | Distant red dwarf companion |
