name: Vesper System
body:
## Overview

The system at the far end of Vesper Reach, dimmer and quieter than Kestrel under its banked orange star. Vesper has no war of its own — what it has is a dying Mandate relay array whose slow collapse is the real reason the Reach has grown so unreliable, and a small waystation now quietly used by nearly every faction with an interest in Kestrel's war as a back channel nobody else is watching too closely.

## Stellar Characteristics

| Star        | Type | Notes                                              |
| ----------- | ---- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Vesper's Eye | K3V  | Dim orange dwarf, noticeably cooler light than Kestrel Primary |

## Planetary Bodies

| Body                  | Type        | Primary? | Notes                                  | Link                    |
| --------------------- | ----------- | -------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| [[Vesper Hollow]]     | Terrestrial | Yes      | Waystation, multi-faction back channel  | [[Vesper Hollow]]        |
| [[Vesper's Shroud]]   | Gas giant   | No       | Faint rings, derelict Mandate relay array | [[Vesper's Shroud]]      |
| [[The Driftfield]]    | Wreck field | No       | Graveyard of failed Reach transits, salvage | [[The Driftfield]]     |

## Space Stations & Facilities

- **The Anchorage** — orbital/surface waystation over Vesper Hollow; the system's only real settlement and its only law, such as it is

## Jump Routes

- [[Vesper Reach]] — 4 days back to [[Kestrel System]]; the route's growing unreliability traces back to the failing Mandate array on [[Vesper's Shroud]]
- The Silent Span — unexplored beyond the jump point

## Factions Present

- [[Kestrel Corporate Council]] — small listening post at the Anchorage, a supply back channel that bypasses Ashvale-contested space
- [[Ashvale Coalition]] — a single embedded infiltrator watching Council traffic
- [[Kestrel Free Traders Association]] — an alternate trade corridor now that the direct Kestrel run has grown dangerous
- [[Red Veil Cartel]] — salvage and smuggling operation working The Driftfield and fencing goods through the Anchorage
- [[Mandate Remnant Surveyors]] — investigating the failing array on [[Vesper's Shroud]] before it either collapses or gets stripped by scavengers

## Points of Interest

- The Vesper Array, the derelict Mandate relay anchored to one of Shroud's moons — see [[Vesper's Shroud]]
- The Anchorage's underlevels, a loose gray market where every faction present pretends not to notice the others

name: Ashvale's Answer
body:
## Overview

A Council gravtank captured whole during an early ambush on a supply convoy through the highland passes — the only one of three taken that day still running. Repainted in Coalition colors and kept alive by scavenged parts and stubborn maintenance crews, it's the single most feared asset either side of the Kestrel II civil war fields on the ground.

## Stats

| Stat          | Value        |
| ------------- | ------------ |
| Vehicle Type  | [[Gravtank]] |
| HP            | 50           |
| Speed         | 2            |
| Armor         | Special      |
| Crew          | 3            |
| Weapon Mounts | 6            |
| TL            | 5            |

## Crew & Passengers

- **Driver/Commander** — Sergeant Yuli Kray, a former Council armor crewman who defected with the regiment
- Two gunners, both highland volunteers trained up from scratch since none of Ashvale's original crews survived the ambush

## Cargo & Notable Gear

- Coalition markings painted directly over the original Council insignia, still faintly visible underneath
- A dwindling stock of TL5 ammunition and spare parts — nothing on Kestrel II can manufacture replacements

## History

- Captured during an ambush on a Council supply convoy moving through the highland passes early in the war
- Has anchored at least two major Coalition victories since, cementing its reputation on both sides

name: Kestrel II
body:
## Overview

The primary world of the Kestrel System and the reason the system matters at all. Kestrel II sits at the crossroads of three jump routes, and Port Kestrel in high orbit has grown into one of the busiest free ports on this stretch of the frontier. The world itself is currently split by an escalating civil war between the old Corporate Council and a breakaway warlord coalition, making the ground below far less safe than the trade lanes above.

## World Stats

| Stat       | Value                                                |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Atmosphere | Breathable                                           |
| Biosphere  | Human-miscible                                       |
| Population | Moderate (4-6 million)                               |
| Tech Level | TL4                                                  |
| Government | Fractured Corporate Council (contested)              |
| World Tags | Colonized Population, Trade Center, Warlord Uprising |

## Geography & Environment

- Two continents: Meridian (Council-held, industrial/coastal) and Ashvale (warlord-held, inland highlands)
- Temperate climate with heavy seasonal storms over the equatorial ocean
- Meridian's coastline is dotted with old orbital-elevator anchor ruins from the Mandate era

## Settlements

- **New Kestrel City** (Meridian) — Council capital, ~1.2 million, orbital elevator terminus
- **Dawnreach** (Meridian) — secondary port city, industrial and shipbuilding
- **Ashvale Hold** (Ashvale) — warlord coalition's fortified seat of power
- Numerous unaligned mining and farming settlements caught between the two factions

## Factions & Notable NPCs

- **[[Kestrel Corporate Council]]** — nominal planetary government, losing ground; based in New Kestrel City
- **[[Ashvale Coalition]]** — warlord alliance seeking independence from Council rule; based in Ashvale Hold
- **[[Kestrel Free Traders Association]]** — neutral merchant guild trying to keep Port Kestrel open to both sides
- **[[Red Veil Cartel]]** — smugglers exploiting the chaos to move contraband and weapons
- [[Governor Lian Osk]] — Council administrator, increasingly desperate to broker outside intervention
- [[Warlord Rurik Ashvale]] — Coalition leader, former Council militia commander

## Trade & Economy

- Primary exports: refined ore from the Shattered Belt, agricultural goods from Meridian
- Port Kestrel functions as the system's economic lifeline; both factions tacitly avoid disrupting it
- War has driven up prices on weapons, medical supplies, and spike drive parts

## Points of Interest

- The abandoned orbital elevator anchors — pretech ruins worth investigating
- New Kestrel City's underlevels, now a haven for refugees and black marketeers
- Ashvale Hold's mountain fortress, built into an old Mandate bunker complex

name: Kestrel III
body:
## Overview

A banded gas giant with a large, brilliant ring system — not a place anyone lives, but the reason half of Kestrel's current troubles exist. One of Kestrel III's moons hides a sealed Mandate-era installation, and the pretech cache inside it is the true source of the military-grade weapons and spike drive components flooding into the Kestrel II civil war.

## World Stats

| Stat       | Value                                    |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Atmosphere | None (gas giant)                          |
| Biosphere  | None                                      |
| Population | None                                      |
| Tech Level | TL5 (derelict Mandate installation only)  |
| Government | None                                      |
| World Tags | Mandate Base                              |

## Geography & Environment

- A banded gas giant with a prominent, richly-colored ring system, easily visible from Kestrel II on a clear night
- A cluster of small moons orbit within and beyond the rings — mostly airless rock, unremarkable except for one
- No stable orbital infrastructure; the rings make close approach hazardous without a skilled pilot

## Settlements

- None. No permanent population, no registered claims — which is exactly why it's gone unnoticed this long

## Factions & Notable NPCs

- **[[Red Veil Cartel]]** — quietly extracting weapons and spike drive components from the vault, disguising the runs as Shattered Belt mining traffic
- **[[Mandate Remnant Surveyors]]** — want the site studied and recovered intact before it's stripped or weaponized further

## Trade & Economy

- No legitimate trade. All economic activity here is the Red Veil Cartel's black-market extraction operation

## Points of Interest

- A sealed Mandate-era vault on one of the moons, the source of the pretech cache — exact moon and access route known only to [[Captain Vashti Kael]] and a handful of her crew

name: Kestrel IV
body:
## Overview

A frozen, wind-scoured world at the edge of Kestrel's habitable zone. Once home to a small research outpost, now dark and unclaimed. Nobody currently in Kestrel System has bothered to find out why it was abandoned or what, if anything, was left behind.

## World Stats

| Stat       | Value                |
| ---------- | --------------------- |
| Atmosphere | Thin                   |
| Biosphere  | None                    |
| Population | None                     |
| Tech Level | TL4 (abandoned)          |
| Government | None                      |
| World Tags | Abandoned Colony          |

## Geography & Environment

- Perpetual ice sheets and glacial plains, with violent katabatic windstorms off the polar caps
- A handful of exposed rock ridges near the equator are the only ground not permanently under ice

## Settlements

- **The Outpost** — a shuttered research station, structurally intact but powered down and unvisited in years

## Factions & Notable NPCs

- None currently active — no faction in Kestrel System has moved to reclaim or investigate it

## Trade & Economy

- None

## Points of Interest

- The abandoned research outpost — sealed, silent, and unexplored by anyone currently in Kestrel

name: The Driftfield
body:
## Overview

A scattered graveyard of wreckage on the outer edge of Vesper System — decades of ships that mistimed a transit through the increasingly unreliable Reach, drifting alongside older hulks nobody can even date. It draws independent scavengers and, more quietly, the Red Veil Cartel, who've made it a forward base for salvage and smuggling far from Port Kestrel's eyes.

## World Stats

| Stat       | Value              |
| ---------- | -------------------- |
| Atmosphere | None                   |
| Biosphere  | None                    |
| Population | Sparse                   |
| Tech Level | TL4 (salvaged mix)         |
| Government | None                          |
| World Tags | Rogue Tech                       |

## Geography & Environment

- Not a true asteroid belt — a loose scatter of ship debris, ice, and rock, thin enough that most of it has to be found by transponder ghost and wreck-diving rather than sight
- Navigation is hazardous; wrecks drift and tumble unpredictably, and older hulks have been known to still carry live ordnance
- Some wreckage is recent — failed Reach transits — but a disturbing amount predates anyone's records of the route being used at all

## Settlements

- None fixed. A handful of scavenger crews work out of patched-together salvage tenders, moving as the pickings dictate

## Factions & Notable NPCs

- [[Red Veil Cartel]] — runs salvage and smuggling operations out of the Driftfield via [[Enforcer Dashiell Corr]] and the [[Widow's Toll]]
- Independent scavenger crews, unaligned and territorial about their claims

## Trade & Economy

- Salvage is the only economy here — scavenged parts, hull plate, and the occasional intact system get sold on through the Anchorage or run back to Kestrel
- Red Veil folds its own smuggling runs into the general scavenger traffic, much as it does with the mining traffic in the Shattered Belt back home

## Points of Interest

- The oldest wrecks in the field, pre-dating any recorded transit of Vesper Reach — nobody has a good explanation for how they got there

name: The Shattered Belt
body:
## Overview

A dense asteroid belt on the outer edge of Kestrel System, worked by independent mining crews and haunted by pirates who prey on the ore haulers. Its constant traffic of unregistered ships and mining transponders makes it the perfect place to hide something you don't want found — which is exactly how the Red Veil Cartel uses it.

## World Stats

| Stat       | Value          |
| ---------- | --------------- |
| Atmosphere | None             |
| Biosphere  | None              |
| Population | Sparse             |
| Tech Level | TL4                 |
| Government | None                 |
| World Tags | Heavy Mining          |

## Geography & Environment

- A dense field of metal-rich asteroids, remnants of a shattered planetoid
- Navigation hazards are constant; only experienced pilots run the Belt without an escort

## Settlements

- **Blackreef Outpost** — independent station, the Belt's only fixed point of law (such as it is) and its main ore transshipment point

## Factions & Notable NPCs

- **[[Red Veil Cartel]]** — operates out of the Belt, using its mining traffic as cover for weapons runs; effectively home base for [[Captain Vashti Kael]] and the [[Nightshade Vow]]
- Independent mining crews and prospectors, mostly unaligned with either side of the Kestrel II civil war

## Trade & Economy

- Refined ore is one of Kestrel II's primary exports, mined here and shipped in through Port Kestrel
- Red Veil's smuggling runs are folded directly into the legitimate ore traffic, making them hard to distinguish without inspecting cargo manifests closely

## Points of Interest

- Blackreef Outpost — independent station, functionally the Belt's capital

name: Vesper Hollow
body:
## Overview

A cold, thin-aired rock that would draw no interest at all if it didn't sit at the far end of Vesper Reach. The Anchorage, its one settlement, has become the quiet back door every faction with a stake in the Kestrel II civil war now uses — a place to move people, supplies, and information around the fighting without anyone back home having to admit they're doing it.

## World Stats

| Stat       | Value                          |
| ---------- | ------------------------------- |
| Atmosphere | Thin                            |
| Biosphere  | Trace (lichen, microbial mats)  |
| Population | Sparse (under 10,000)           |
| Tech Level | TL3 (TL5 salvage circulates)    |
| Government | None (independent waystation)   |
| World Tags | Interstellar Nexus, Offworld Interests |

## Geography & Environment

- A wind-scoured basin ringed by low, cracked mountains gives the world its name — the Anchorage sits in the deepest part of the Hollow, sheltered from the worst of the surface winds
- Native life is limited to hardy lichen and microbial mats; nothing edible, nothing dangerous
- Vesper's Eye sits low and orange on the horizon even at midday, giving the whole settlement a permanent dusk-lit cast

## Settlements

- **The Anchorage** — a patchwork of docking gantries, pressurized modules, and salvaged Mandate-hull sections grown organically over decades; equal parts customs post, black market, and refugee waypoint

## Factions & Notable NPCs

- [[Kestrel Corporate Council]] — a discreet listening post and supply relay, run by [[Warden Petra Voss]]
- [[Ashvale Coalition]] — a single embedded infiltrator, [[Corporal Nyssa Thorne]], watching Council traffic under cover
- [[Kestrel Free Traders Association]] — [[Captain Joss Merrin]] and the [[Wayward Cairn]] run the alternate corridor through here
- [[Red Veil Cartel]] — fences salvage and contraband through the Anchorage's underlevels via [[Enforcer Dashiell Corr]]
- [[Mandate Remnant Surveyors]] — [[Field Archivist Sela Brint]] passes through here en route to the array on [[Vesper's Shroud]]

## Trade & Economy

- No local production to speak of; the Anchorage lives entirely on transit fees, salvage from The Driftfield, and quiet favors between factions who'd rather not be seen dealing with each other back in Kestrel
- Prices run high on anything that isn't scavenged — every finished good has to come in through the Reach

## Points of Interest

- The Anchorage's underlevels, where Red Veil's fencing operation and half the settlement's real business happens out of sight of the docking gantries
- A row of sealed Mandate-hull sections built into the settlement's oldest quarter — nobody's fully catalogued what's inside them

name: Vesper's Shroud
body:
## Overview

A banded gas giant wrapped in a faint, ash-colored ring, easy to miss next to Kestrel III's brighter cousin back home. What matters isn't the planet — it's the derelict Mandate relay array anchored to one of its moons, a jump-calibration station that once helped stabilize transit through Vesper Reach and is now, after centuries of neglect, slowly failing. That failure is the true cause of the Reach's growing unreliability.

## World Stats

| Stat       | Value                                     |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Atmosphere | None (gas giant)                            |
| Biosphere  | None                                         |
| Population | None                                          |
| Tech Level | TL5 (derelict Mandate installation only)       |
| Government | None                                             |
| World Tags | Mandate Base, Sealed Menace                        |

## Geography & Environment

- A dim, ash-banded gas giant with a faint ring system, far less striking than Kestrel III's
- A handful of small moons; the array is anchored to the largest, a cratered rock locals call the Cairn
- No stable approach without accounting for the array's failing navigation beacons, which throw stray ships' instruments off without warning

## Settlements

- None. The array was never meant to be inhabited — only tended, and it hasn't been tended in a very long time

## Factions & Notable NPCs

- [[Mandate Remnant Surveyors]] — [[Field Archivist Sela Brint]] is stationed here investigating the array's decline before it fails completely or draws scavenger attention
- [[Red Veil Cartel]] — avoids the array itself but uses the navigational dead zones it creates to slip patrols near The Driftfield

## Trade & Economy

- None directly, though the array's instability is indirectly responsible for a great deal of Vesper Reach's smuggling traffic — patrols give the area a wide berth

## Points of Interest

- The Vesper Array — a sprawling Mandate-era relay and jump-calibration station built into the Cairn, its outer sections open to vacuum and its core still drawing power from a source nobody has identified
